title: RAW_UNSCREENED: okaiin-Wiederaufnahme als Träger oder Registerkopf
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: f29v.4 repeats okaiin around cthy oltchy; the repeat may conserve one material carrier through a state block or reopen an independent record field.

design.scope_description: Exact f29v.4 and f21r.9 okaiin contexts in GDT809/GDT625; no cross-page identity assumption.
design.mechanism: Carrier-reuse reading binds the two okaiin occurrences to one local participant; record reading treats them as repeated whole-form heads.
design.unit: f29v.4 okaiin cthy oltchy ... okaiin plus f21r.9 okaiin context.
design.contrast: Conserved participant versus independent record-head reuse.
design.prediction: Carrier reuse predicts one written state transition between the two occurrences and compatible input/output attributes; independent-head reading predicts each occurrence can have separate cofields and no identity link.
concrete_observations: f29v.4 contains okaiin before cthy oltchy and again at line end.
GDT809 explicitly notes repeated okaiin does not prove same preparation or batch.
linked_consequences: A conserved carrier must retain a single identity through the intervening block.
A record-head interpretation should find the same whole form in independent entry positions without requiring state continuity.
design.nearest_rival: Parallel profile heads with accidental identical spelling.
design.distinguishing_observation: Require a written attribute/output relation between the two f29v occurrences; absence leaves the identity model unselected, while independent recurrence elsewhere supports the rival.
assumption_costs: carrier identity is a whole-form hypothesis
design.strongest_likely_failure: The single line has no independent identity marker, so recurrence remains compatible with both readings.
